extracted.intended_audience: Attorneys/practitioners who represent trademark applicants or registrants before the USPTO (especially U.S.-licensed counsel for foreign-domiciled parties)
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order describing the professional conduct rules, certifications, signature rules, supervisory duties, sanctions, and reinstatement/notification requirements applicable to practitioners who file trademark matters before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction to discipline practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26, 11.32, and 11.39.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the statutory and regulatory basis for OED disciplinary proceedings and Final Orders against practitioners who represent parties before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Counsel Rule (37 C.F.R. § 2.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective August 3, 2019, any foreign-domiciled trademark applicant or registrant must be represented before the USPTO by an attorney licensed to practice law in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule intended to increase compliance with U.S. trademark law, improve accuracy of submissions, and safeguard the integrity of the U.S. trademark register (84 Fed. Reg. 31498).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications when presenting papers (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner certifies that all statements made on his or her own knowledge are true, and that all statements based on the practitioner's information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline truthfulness certification required whenever presenting (signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) any paper to the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive certification requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner certifies that, to the best of the party's knowledge, information and belief, formed after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances: (i) the paper is not presented for an improper purpose; (ii) legal contentions are warranted by existing law or nonfrivolous argument; (iii) allegations and factual contentions have evidentiary support or are likely to after reasonable investigation; and (iv) denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence or reasonably based on lack of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes both legal and factual responsibility: filings must not be to harass/delay; legal theories must be nonfrivolous; factual assertions must be supported or reasonably investigable. The phrase 'inquiry reasonable under the circumstances' is central to determining adequacy of the practitioner's pre-filing investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner presenting any paper to the USPTO certifies that he has conducted an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances that supports the factual assertions set forth in the paper (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to perform such a reasonable inquiry can constitute misrepresentation and other professional conduct violations; the Order cites examples (e.g., spending only a few minutes preparing, signing, and filing responses) as evidence of inadequate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO trademark signature rules (37 C.F.R. §§ 2.193(a),(c),(e) and 11.18(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All signatures on trademark documents must be signed by a proper person; documents must be personally signed by the signatory named on the document; electronic signatory must personally enter the adopted signature between two forward slashes ("/").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic signature requires the signatory to manually enter the combination of letters/numbers/spaces/punctuation and place it between slashes in the signature block. Failure to comply affects execution validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMEP guidance on personal signing (TMEP § 611.01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents must be personally signed; the person identified as the signatory must manually enter the elements of the electronic signature. Another person (e.g., paralegal, legal assistant, or secretary) may not sign the name of a qualified practitioner or other authorized signatory. Typing another's electronic signature is not a valid signature by that person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces that surrogate signing or typing another person's signature is impermissible; analogous to handwritten signature rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of impermissible signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the signature on a trademark application or other submission fails to comply because it was entered by someone other than the named signatory or not signed by a proper person, then the submission is improperly executed, cannot be relied upon to support registration, and normally renders the application void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improperly executed filings adversely affect the integrity of the federal trademark registration process; prior USPTO disciplinary cases cited (e.g., In re Yusha Zhang; In re Dermahose Inc.; Ex parte Hipkins; In re Cowan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities regarding non-practitioner assistance (37 C.F.R. § 11.503(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must adequately supervise or ensure reliability of information gathered by non-practitioners for trademark applications; authorizing/allowing non-practitioners to gather information without adequate supervision violates §11.503(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on foreign-located trademark service companies or other third parties, practitioners must take reasonable steps to ensure that the information (e.g., assertions of use, specimens) is credible and reliable before presenting it to the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence obligation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall provide competent representation; includes understanding and complying with obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18 before presenting filings to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serving as U.S. counsel requires knowledge of applicable professional conduct rules; lacking such understanding can constitute a violation of competence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence obligation (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must act with diligence, including taking reasonable steps to ensure clients' filings are prepared in accordance with laws, rules, and regulations and reviewing and signing certifications only after conducting an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances (violations of §11.18 implicate §11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to take such steps (e.g., insufficient review prior to signing) is a breach of diligence and may lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation prohibition (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in misrepresentation by signing documents and impliedly falsely certifying that a reasonable inquiry was conducted when, in fact, it was not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit false certification through signature is actionable; the Order treats signing without reasonable inquiry as misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to USPTO administration (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of the USPTO trademark registration system by failing to ensure filings were prepared in accordance with applicable laws and by signing certifications without conducting a reasonable inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conduct undermines the trademark registration process and is a separate enumerated basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other conduct reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in other conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO—for example, serving as U.S. counsel for approximately 15,000 trademark matters as a solo practitioner without adequate systems to satisfy duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume of representation without adequate safeguards may itself be an aggravating factor bearing on fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office for a period of six (6) months and remains suspended until a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order sets a specific suspension length and ties reinstatement to regulatory petition process under §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties upon suspension/withdrawal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, including notice and transfer obligations for clients and matters affected by suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order specifies detailed methods for providing the §11.58 notices to foreign-domiciled clients (e.g., emailing notices in client's native language, including translated Final Order) and sets conditions when notices are sent via referring third parties (reasonable measures, verification, affidavit details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification for foreign-domiciled clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may satisfy § 11.58(c)(3)(i) for foreign clients by emailing the requisite notices and information (including a correctly translated copy of the Final Order) to: (1) the client's email address listed in the application if it belongs to the client and the respondent reasonably believes the client has direct access; (2) an email address belonging to the client to which respondent reasonably believes the client has direct access; or (3) the referring foreign-domiciled third person/entity only if respondent takes reasonable measures to ensure the client actually receives the email and translated Final Order and documents this in an affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on intermediaries, Respondent must (A) ensure forwarding and copy; (B) verify client receipt; (C) set forth reasonable measures in §11.58(d) affidavit; and (D) include details in any reinstatement petition. These are concrete supervision/verification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to conclude matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition for thirty (30) days starting on the date of the Final Order so he may endeavor to conclude work on pending matters; if work cannot be concluded within 30 days, Respondent must so advise each client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow, time-limited exception to suspension to allow orderly wind-down of active matters; after 30 days limitations/disablement of accounts apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO account restrictions and disabling
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective after the 30-day limited-recognition period, the USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to Respondent. Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to any USPTO verified Electronic System account until reinstated. Respondent is prohibited from using or assisting others in using any USPTO.gov accounts for preparing or filing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also authorizes USPTO to disallow respondent from verifying others' credentials, sponsoring accounts, or re-activating disabled accounts without respondent initiating re-activation; violation can lead to further disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with USPTO investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall cooperate fully with the USPTO in any present or future inquiry into improper filings by specified foreign-located trademark service companies or any other third-party entities with whom Respondent worked or was solicited to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation is an affirmative condition of the settlement and may be enforced during probation or reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation term and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed and terminating twelve (12) months after a decision by the OED Director granting a petition for reinstatement to practice in trademark and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation includes active monitoring and reporting requirements and may be used to trigger further action if violations occur during the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedure for probation violations (Order to Show Cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director, in good faith, believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's last address of record, and grant Respondent 15 days to respond. If noncompliance remains after response, the OED Director may deliver materials to the USPTO Director and request immediate additional suspension up to six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural steps and timelines for imposing further suspension for probation violations and reserve right to seek discrete discipline for misconduct forming the basis of the Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and reporting duties while on probation
rubrics_metrics.description: While on probation Respondent shall, at least on a bi-weekly basis, (i) search the USPTO's online trademark search system for applications identifying him as the attorney of record and (ii) promptly inform in writing the USPTO Office of Trademark Examination Policy of each trademark document filing identifying him as the attorney of record that was made without his knowledge or consent. Additionally, at least on a bi-monthly basis Respondent shall submit a written report to the OED Director stating that he has completed a monthly search and either (i) identified no improper filings or (ii) provided copies of correspondence sent to the Office of Trademark Examination Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual-frequency obligations (bi-weekly searches and bi-monthly reports that reference monthly searches) are mandated; reports must document searches and any corrective notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement prerequisites (CLE and TMEP review)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of being reinstated, Respondent must provide an affidavit/declaration (per 28 U.S.C. § 1746) stating that he has successfully completed four (4) hours of continuing legal education credit on ethics/professional responsibility and that he has thoroughly reviewed all provisions of the TMEP, including the USPTO's signature requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires both training (documented CLE) and demonstrable familiarity with USPTO procedural guidance (TMEP). Reinstatement petition must also set forth details about reasonable measures taken when notices were sent through third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the Order's notice of suspension and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure of discipline and supporting facts is required and can be considered in future proceedings as aggravating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior discipline in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) in any future complaint or disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as (1) an aggravating factor, (2) to rebut statements by or on Respondent's behalf, and/or (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past discipline is explicitly preserved as relevant evidence in later enforcement or reinstatement matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of appellate/reconsideration rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural element of this settlement disposing of rights to challenge the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No prevailing-party costs award; settlement allocates expenses to each party.
